source.body: ### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? 26.707.72221 (build 5307) ### What subscription do you have? ChatGPT Plus ### What platform is your computer? Fedora Linux 43 uname -mprs: Linux 7.2.11-100.fc43.x86_64 x86_64 unknown ### What issue are you seeing? Codex repeatedly replaces responses with this message: “This content can't be shown We take extra caution with cybersecurity requests. If you’re a security professional, you may be able to apply for Trusted Access.” The affected conversation includes local application development, UI changes, API connection troubleshooting, and bug-bounty automation requests. The notice also appeared when I asked why responses were being hidden and how to resolve the access problem. This makes it difficult to troubleshoot or understand what work is permitted. I attempted the Trusted Access application process, but I cannot confirm that access was successfully enabled. Please investigate whether ordinary explanatory follow-ups are being incorrectly blocked. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. Open the affected existing task in Codex App. 2. Continue the application-development conversation. 3. After the safety notice appears, ask why it appeared and what steps can resolve it. 4. Observe that the explanatory response can also be replaced by the same notice. This was observed repeatedly in the existing conversation. Reproduction in a fresh conversation has not been confirmed. Feedback/task ID: 01a16499-33f8-7683-91fa-b1b9c4e41831 Token and context-window usage at the exact failures: unknown. ### What is the expected behavior? Permitted troubleshooting and explanatory questions should receive useful answers. When a request is restricted, provide clear guidance about the restriction, relevant access requirements, and how to report a possible mistake or recover the task. ### Additional information A screenshot of the repeated notice is attached. Please check whether Trusted Access is enabled for my account and whether the affected task has a persistent classification or access problem. Private credentials and project details are omitted.
